cards.text: The three visitors Abraham just fed under his tree get up to leave, and they look out over the city of Sodom. Abraham walks along with them to see them off. These days most of us see a guest off by yelling "BYE" from the couch, so give this man some credit.
Then the LORD asks, "Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?" Friend, when you hear a line like THAT, you put the cookie down and you lean in.

cards.question: The LORD says Abraham will surely become a great and powerful nation, and through him all the ___ of the earth will be blessed.
True or false: The LORD says He chose Abraham so Abraham would lead his children and his household to do what is right and just.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks about two cities, Sodom and Gomorrah. The outcry against them is great, and their sin is so grievous.

cards.question: With an outcry that great against Sodom and Gomorrah, what does the LORD say He will do?

answers.text: Go down and see if their actions fit the outcry
Send a messenger to warn them one more time
Leave the two cities alone until next year

cards.text: The two men turn away and head toward Sodom, but Abraham stays right there, standing before the LORD. Everybody else is leaving, and Abraham is planted like a man with one more thing to say.

cards.question: Abraham steps forward to speak to the LORD about Sodom. What does he ask?

answers.text: Will You sweep away the righteous with the wicked
Will You let me go down there with the two men
Will You tell me the day Sarah's son will come

cards.text: Then Abraham puts a number out there: what if there are fifty righteous people in the city, will the LORD still sweep it away and not spare the place for their sake? Abraham is NEGOTIATING, friend, and I couldn't even haggle my way down from my own 25-cent price sticker.

cards.question: True or false: Abraham tells the LORD it would be fine for the righteous and the wicked to be treated alike.

cards.text: Then Abraham says, "Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?" That's a BOLD question, friend, and he asks it with his whole chest.

cards.question: The LORD answers Abraham about fifty righteous people in Sodom. What will the LORD do if He finds them?

answers.text: Spare the whole place on their account
Rescue the fifty and let the city fall
Give the city one more year to change

cards.text: Abraham speaks up again, and this time he calls himself "but dust and ashes." Friend, I spent YEARS covered in junk drawer dust, and Abraham still out-humbled me.

cards.question: Abraham asks what happens if the fifty righteous people are five short. True or false: The LORD says if He finds forty-five there, He will not destroy the city.

cards.text: Abraham asks about forty, and the LORD says on account of the forty He won't do it. Then Abraham asks the Lord not to be angry, and he goes down to thirty.

cards.question: True or false: When Abraham asks about thirty righteous people in Sodom, the LORD says thirty isn't enough to spare the city.
After thirty, Abraham speaks to the Lord again and goes lower. What number of righteous people does he ask about next?

cards.text: The LORD answers that on account of the twenty, He will not destroy it. Fifty, forty-five, forty, thirty, TWENTY, friend, this man is working those numbers like a clearance rack on the last day of the sale!

cards.question: Abraham asks the Lord not to be angry and says he'll speak just once more. He asks what if only ___ righteous people are found in Sodom.

cards.text: The LORD answers, "On account of the ten, I will not destroy it." Then He departs, Abraham heads home, and friend, keep that apron on, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 13 quotes "but dust and ashes.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says the three visitors are the ones 'Abraham just fed under his tree.' That fact comes from Genesis 18:1-8, but the card cites only Genesis 18:16 and gives no reference for it. Also, 'his tree' says the tree is Abraham's, and the text just calls it 'the tree' (18:4, 8).

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to supply the next word of the LORD's line ('all the ___ of the earth will be blessed'). That tests wording, not meaning. No story card before it sets up this promise, so 'nations' over 'kings' or 'cities' comes down to recalling or guessing the wording.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The statement says Abraham would 'lead' his children and household. The text says he will 'command' them to keep the way of the LORD (Genesis 18:19). 'Lead' softens what the text calls it.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question says Abraham speaks to the LORD 'about Sodom.' That rules out the wrong answer 'Will You tell me the day Sarah's son will come,' which has nothing to do with Sodom.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Will You sweep away the righteous with the wicked' uses Bible-sounding words ('sweep away,' 'righteous,' 'wicked'). The two wrong answers are plain everyday wording, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The joke 'I couldn't even haggle my way down from my own 25-cent price sticker' doesn't click. Papa Dorin was the item for sale, so haggling down his own price makes no sense, and a stranger would say 'huh?' It also calls back to the 25-cent sticker, which hasn't been set up earlier in this lesson.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The card says 'Abraham asks the Lord not to be angry.' The text has Abraham saying, 'May the Lord not be angry' (Genesis 18:30). Turning a 'May the Lord…' line into a request is exactly the pattern the rule's example marks as wrong.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question says 'Abraham asks the Lord not to be angry.' The text has Abraham saying, 'May the Lord not be angry' (Genesis 18:32). This is the same 'May the Lord…' to request change that the rule's example marks as wrong.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Card 1 says 'three visitors' and card 7 says 'the two men' head toward Sodom while Abraham stands before the LORD. No card connects the two counts, so a baker may wonder where the third visitor went. The text implies the LORD is the one who stays (Genesis 18:1-2, 22), but the docs say both to fill in what the text clearly implies and to leave open what the text leaves open.
findings.question: Should Prep say plainly that the LORD was one of the three visitors and is the one who stays with Abraham, or leave the shift from three to two unexplained?
